STORY CONTEXT — read by the runtime before your first turn, through the same
governed tools you use, and recorded in the ledger. Do not read these items
again. Anything this runtime wrote itself has already been removed.

STORY AB#111 [User Story, New] Customer sorts the product list
Acceptance criteria:
  • AC-1: The list is sorted by name from A to Z when it first opens. 
  • AC-2: Sorting by name from Z to A reverses that order. 
  • AC-3: Sorting by price from low to high lists the cheapest product first, and from high to low the most expensive first.
Description:
  As a customer I want to sort the products by name or price.
EXISTING TEST CASES (4) — one per acceptance criterion is the rule. Do NOT create another case for a criterion listed here; the runtime refuses a duplicate:
  #140 AC-1 Product list is sorted A to Z by name when it first opens
  #141 AC-2 Sorting by name Z to A reverses the order
  #142 AC-3 Sorting by price lists the cheapest or most expensive product first
  #143 AC-story Product list page passes accessibility checks

PARENT #106 [Epic] Product list
  The list of products, sorting it, a product's own page, and adding from the list.

OTHER STORIES UNDER THIS EPIC — behaviour that belongs to one of these is NOT this story's to test. If an open bug below is about one of them, say so and leave it:
  #112 [User Story] Customer opens a product's own page
    • AC-1: Choosing a product's name in the list opens its page with the same name, description and price as in the list. 
    • AC-2: Adding the product from its page changes the button to Remove and the cart shows 1. 
    • AC-3: Back to products returns to the product list.
  #113 [User Story] Customer adds and removes products from the list
    • AC-1: Adding a product from the list changes its button to Remove and the cart badge shows the number of products added. 
    • AC-2: Removing it changes the button back to Add to cart and lowers the cart badge; with nothing left the badge is not shown. 
    • AC-3: Products added stay in the cart after moving to another page and back.
  #119 [User Story] Every product shows its own picture
    • AC-1: Each product in the list shows a picture, and no two products show the same picture. 
    • AC-2: A product's picture on its own page is the same as in the list.

CHILD ITEMS: none linked to this story.

COMMENTS — 0 from people:
  (none)

OPEN BUGS — 2 filed by people.
Each state asks something different of you:
  #121 [Active] Problem user sees the same picture for every product
    ACTIVE — known broken and being worked. A test for it is EXPECTED to fail; that failure is not a new defect and must not become a bug.
    Steps: sign in as the problem user and look at the product list. 
    EXPECTED: each product shows its own picture. 
    ACTUAL: every product shows the same picture. 
    Filed by a person, not by attestqa.
  #122 [Active] Error user cannot finish an order
    ACTIVE — known broken and being worked. A test for it is EXPECTED to fail; that failure is not a new defect and must not become a bug.
    Steps: sign in as the error user, add a product, check out, fill in the details, finish. 
    EXPECTED: the thank-you message. 
    ACTUAL: the order is not completed (the exact symptom to be confirmed on the day: a field that does not take input, or Finish that does nothing). 
    Filed by a person, not by attestqa.

For EACH open bug above, say in one line whether it touches THIS story's
behaviour and why. Relevance is your judgement: a bug about a neighbouring
story is not a reason to add a test here, and saying so is a finding.
